headline: Approved alcohol service permit for a 20-room hotel at 349 Main Street, and cottage additions at 240 Cards Pond Road.
summary: Six applications were approved, including alcohol service at a 20-room hotel and several cottage projects at Roy Carpenter's Beach. Three appeals were continued: the Lavender Waves Farm appeal to March 17, 2027, and two Columbia Street and Frank Avenue appeals to November 18, 2026.

Approved a special use permit to allow alcohol service at the hotel at 349 Main Street, 5-0.
Approved a special use permit for a 168 sq. ft. addition to the cottage at 240 Cards Pond Road, 4-1.
Approved a dimensional variance for the cottage addition at 240 Cards Pond Road, 4-1.
Approved a dimensional variance for multiple additions to the home at 135 Park Avenue, 5-0.
Approved a special use permit to replace the cottage at 240 Cards Pond Road with a 572 sq. ft. cottage, 5-0.
Approved a dimensional variance for a garage addition at 83 Quagnut Drive, 5-0.
Approved a special use permit to enclose an existing deck at the cottage at 240 Cards Pond Road, 5-0.
Continued the appeal of the zoning enforcement decision at 84 Frank Avenue to November 18, 2026, 5-0.
Continued the appeal of the zoning enforcement decision at 28 Columbia Street to November 18, 2026, 5-0.

# Town of South Kingstown

## Zoning Board of Review Meeting

Meeting Minutes

Wednesday, October 21, 2026 at 7:00 PM

South Kingstown Town Hall, Town Council Chambers

180 High Street, Wakefield, RI 02879

www.southkingstownri.gov

Robert Cagnetta, Chair

Thomas Daniels, Vice Chair

Arlene Hicks, Member

Geoff Elia, Member

William MacDonald, Member

Vacancy, Alt. #1

Vacancy, Alt. #2

Vacancy, Alt. #3

### A. Call to Order

This month's meeting agenda includes the applications from the September 16th Zoning Board of Review Meeting, which was canceled due to a lack of quorum.

Mr. Cagnetta called the meeting to order at 7:03:21 PM.

### B. Chairman Introductions and Instructions

Mr. Cagnetta explained the rules and procedures.

**Members Present:** Robert Cagnetta, Chairman; Thomas Daniels, Vice Chairman; Arlene Hicks, Member; Geoff Elia, Member; William MacDonald, Member.

**Members Absent:** None

**Staff Present:** Amy Goins, Town Legal Counsel; Jamie Gorman, Building and Zoning Official; Ben Barbera, Building and Zoning Associate.

Members voting tonight will be Mr. Cagnetta, Mr. Daniels, Ms. Hicks, Mr. Elia and Mr. MacDonald.

### C. Agenda Items *Order can be subject to change*

Mr. Cagnetta called for the first petition.

- I. **Continuation of petition ZA-26-1: Henry Cabrera**, 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway, Wakefield, RI 02879, for an Appeal under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking to **Appeal a Notice of Violation issued by the Zoning Enforcement Officer (ZEO)**, dated May 22, 2025, related to premises at 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway. The owner of the property is Henry Cabrera, for premises located at 3812 Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry Highway, South Kingstown, Assessor's Map 78-3, Lot 7 and is zoned R200.

3812 Comm. O. H. Hwy. - Application

All the material was recognized and entered into the record.

This petition is continued from the August 19, 2026, Zoning Board of Review meeting.

Attorney Stephen Angell was present, representing Henry Cabera and Lavender Waves Farm.

Also, present is Ed Pimentel, who is a planner and land use expert.

The board's main concern discussed during the last meeting was about advertising non-farming-related events on Lavender Waves Farm's website.

Attorney Angell is seeking an accessory use for the principal use of Lavender Waves Farm's property, primarily related to wedding events.

The application is currently going through a Development Plan Review, which has been taking some time. The application is also going through CRMC review because of wetlands located on the property. In June, Jamie Rabbitt, Dept. Head of Planning, told the applicants that the application was now under administrative review. The applicants are currently waiting for a traffic study that was done for a curb cut. Lavender Waves Farm is currently a functioning farm with farming events and is open on weekends during the season between 9-5pm most days. The DPR process can not be completed until CRMC has given their feedback.

Jamie Gorman reads the original Notice of Violation that was issued in May 2025. The town was made aware that there were advertisements for weddings, anniversaries, and corporate events for the property on Lavender Waves Farm's website. The notice required the owner to make an application to the DPR. In the event that they hosted one of these non-farming events, they would be in violation, subject to fines, and a potential municipal court summons. The zoning ordinance requires any non-agricultural events associated with a farm to be vetted through the development plan review process.

Mr. Angell had asked for a continuance until they have received a determination from CRMC.

Mr. Cagnetta explains that at the last zoning meeting the board was mainly concerned with advertising non-farming events.

Mr. Elia adds that the board requested that the non-farming-related advertisements be removed from Lavender Waves Farm's website. As of the day of this meeting, the advertisements still remain.

Mr. Angell refutes that his client is advertising prospective use of the property in hopes that he gets approval. If the applicants receive booking requests, they will have to cancel them.

Ms. Goins advises the board that a continuance should be approved because the DPR process is taking so long due to no fault of the property owner. It is not a violation of the zoning ordinance to advertise.

At this point, Mr. Angell requested a renewal for continuance. Currently, there is no time frame for when CRMC will review this application. Mr. Angell tells the board that he wants to keep them informed on the DPR process during the next few months.

Mr. Cagnetta recommends that the petition be continued to March of next year, before the season starts, if the DPR and CRMC process is not resolved by then. He also asks for an affidavit from the property owners saying that they understand the regulations and that non-farming events will not take place prior to any agreement with the town.

Mr. Angell agrees and says he will talk to his client.

Ms. Goins adds that if the DPR application is approved, the appeal is going to be withdrawn.

There were no further board questions.

Whereas the following motion was made.

**The motion is as follows:**

**The following motion to continue the petition to the March 17, 2027, Zoning Board of Review Meeting was made by Mr. Cagnetta and duly seconded by Mr. Elia.**

**Motion passed unanimously: (5-0 Vote in favor)**

**(Mr. Cagnetta -Aye, Mr. Elia -Aye, Mr. MacDonald -Aye, Mr. Daniels -Aye, Ms. Hicks -Aye)**

Mr. Cagnetta called for the next petition.

- II. **Petition ZBR-26-28: Room 13, LLC**, P.O. Box 8163, Warwick, RI 02888, requests a Special Use Permit under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking a Special Use Permit to allow alcohol service within the proposed hotel. Lot size is .13 acre. **A Special Use Permit is required per Zoning Ordinance Section 301 (Schedule of Use Regulations Table), Section 504.18 (Standards for Restaurant with Alcohol), and Section 907 (Standards of Relief)**. Owner of the property is 349 Main Street, LLC, for premises located at 349 Main Street, South Kingstown, Assessor's Map 56-3, Lot 48 and is zoned CD (Commercial Downtown).

349 Main Street - Application

All the material was recognized and entered into the record.

David Johnston, attorney, was present and represented the applicants.

Mr. Johnston begins by saying that the applicants are seeking a special use permit for the property that has already been approved for renovations to become a 20-room hotel. The applicants are seeking a liquor license from the town council and, as part of that, they will need a special use permit from this zoning board. The liquor license is primarily for the lobby area of the hotel. As part of the development plan review approval, there is a restriction that alcohol can only be served to hotel guests. Parking and things of that nature were already addressed during the DPR approval.

Mr. Cagnetta inquired as to how compliance with the restriction limiting alcohol service to registered hotel guests only would be monitored and enforced.

Mr. Johnston says that the lobby only contains seven barstools and 21 lounge seats, so a large event could not take place. The lobby is not like your typical bar, it mainly consists of lounge chairs and not table seating.

Mr. Cagnetta asked Mr. Johnston whether the intent was to hold any events in the lobby. Would there be an event room?

Mr. Johnston answers that the special use permit would include hotel rooms and the lobby. Events would not be allowed inside the hotel.

Mr. Daniels expressed concerns regarding how the sale and distribution of alcoholic beverages to the public would be regulated and enforced. Mr. Daniels questioned whether the proposed use would also result in an increased demand for parking in the surrounding area.

Ms. Goins explains that this is a special type of liquor license that only a hotel can receive. The town can place reasonable conditions on a liquor license. The applicant has already agreed to only serve alcoholic beverages to guests only during the planning approval.

Mr. Johnston says it would be up to the staff to make sure that only guests can order alcoholic beverages. The planning department has already approved the 20-room hotel's parking. The intent of the restriction prohibiting the service of alcoholic beverages to the public is to limit the number of individuals accessing the hotel's lobby. By not enforcing the conditions for approval, the hotel could get shut down and lose revenue.

Ms. Goins asserts that the parking requirements are driven simply by the primary use of the hotel. No extra parking is needed for this special use permit to be approved.

Ms. Hicks asked if there were any plans to serve food?

John Brito was present and sworn in.

Mr. Brito confirmed that food service would be provided. He explained that the plans depict a room above the bar designated for food preparation. Food would be served exclusively to hotel guests waiting in the lobby.

Mr. Johnston explains that, two and a half years ago, the planning department did not know the full extent to what the hotel's uses would be.

Mr. Daniels reads the planning board's approval which clearly states that the interior area proposed for food and service shall not be open to the public. The board assumes that "food" includes liquor.

Mr. Cagnetta asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak regarding this petition?

There was no one in the audience who wished to speak in favor or in opposition to the petition.

There were no further board questions.

Whereas the following motion was made.

**The motion is as follows:**

**The following motion to approve the petition was made by Mr. Elia and duly seconded by Ms. Hicks.**

**Motion passed unanimously: (5-0 Vote in favor)**

**(Mr. Elia -Aye, Ms. Hicks -Aye, Mr. Cagnetta -Aye, Mr. MacDonald -Aye, Mr. Daniels -Aye)**

At a meeting held on October 21, 2026, a motion was made to approve the petition regarding **ZBR-26-28: Room 13, LLC**, P.O. Box 8163, Warwick, RI 02888, requests a Special Use Permit under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking a Special Use Permit to allow alcohol service within the proposed hotel. Lot size is .13 acre. **A Special Use Permit is required per Zoning Ordinance Section 301 (Schedule of Use Regulations Table), Section 504.18 (Standards for Restaurant with Alcohol), and Section 907 (Standards of Relief).** Owner of the property is 349 Main Street, LLC, for premises located at 349 Main Street, South Kingstown, Assessor's Map 56-3, Lot 48 and is zoned CD (Commercial Downtown).

**The following individuals spoke as representatives of the applicant:**

- David Johnston, attorney representing the applicant.
- John Brito

**There was no one in the audience who wished to speak in favor or in opposition to the petition.**

**The following materials were entered into the record:**

- "Proposed Liquor Service Areas — Floor Plan" designed by McGeorge Architecture Interiors and dated July 31, 2026; "Final Plan Review" signed by James D. Rabbitt dated April 7, 2026.
- 200' Abutter's List and Radius Map; Legal Notices; and Notarized Affidavit of Mailing.

**Findings of Fact:**

1. The Board finds that the special use is specifically authorized by this Ordinance, because the special use permit will enhance the newly renovated hotel services, capabilities and amenities. Alcohol will be served to hotel guests only, along with a limited food service.

2. The Board finds that the proposed special use satisfies the applicable criteria set forth in Section 504.18, Standards for Restaurant with Alcohol, and Section 907, Standards of Relief, the board acknowledges that the requested liquor license is a specialized license available exclusively to hotels.

3. The Board finds that granting of the special use permit will not alter the general character of the surrounding area or impair the intent or purpose of this Ordinance or the Comprehensive Plan of the Town. In so doing, the Board has considered whether or not satisfactory provisions and arrangements have been or will be made concerning, but not limited to, the following matters, where applicable:

i. Ingress and egress to the lot and to existing or proposed structures thereon with particular reference to automotive and pedestrian safety and convenience, traffic flow and control, and access in case of fire, emergency, or catastrophe; the hotel's proposed renovation plans have been approved by the South Kingstown Building Department. *A Final Plan Review, Minor Land Development Project with Unified Development Review* for the conversion of a former retail store for use as a hotel has been approved by the South Kingstown Planning Department.

ii. Off-street parking and loading areas where required, with particular attention to the items in subsection A.1., above, and the noise, glare, or odor effects of the special use permit on adjoining lots; there is public parking available in the surrounding area.

iii. Trash, storage, and delivery areas with a particular reference to the items in (i) and (ii) above; are not a reasonable concern.

iv. Utilities, with reference to locations, availability, and compatibility are not a reasonable concern.

v. Screening and buffering with reference to type, dimensions, and character are not a reasonable concern.

vi. Signs, if any, and exterior lighting with reference to glare, traffic safety, and compatibility and harmony with lots in the zoning district; signage was not discussed during the meeting.

vii. Required yards and other open space; are not a reasonable concern.

viii. General compatibility with lots in the same or abutting zoning districts; is not a reasonable concern.

**Approval is conditional subject to the following conditions:**

- The board imposes all eight (8) conditions outlined in the *Final Plan Review, Minor Land Development Project with Unified Development Review*, approved by the South Kingstown Planning Department and signed by Administrative Officer James D. Rabbit on April 7, 2026, as conditions of this special use permit.

Mr. Cagnetta called for the next petition.

- III. **Petition ZBR-26-31: Joshua Smith**, 45 West Greenville Rd, Greenville, RI 02828, requests a Special Use Permit and Dimensional Variance under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking to construct a 168 sq. ft. addition to the existing seasonal cottage. The addition will exceed 50% of the floor area that existed in the year 2000, therefore relief of 40 sq. ft.is requested. Lot size is 50.2 acres. **A Special Use Permit is required per Zoning Ordinance Section 203 (Special Use Permit for Addition, Enlargement, Expansion or Intensification) and Section 907 (Standards of Relief). A Dimensional Variance is required per Section 608 (Coastal Community Overlay District)**. Owners of cottage 3E C10 are Joshua & Beth Smith, on property owned by RCB Inc, located at 240 Cards Pond Road, South Kingstown, Assessor's Map 92-1, Lot 9-38 and is zoned R200.

R C BCH R3E C10 - Application

All the material was recognized and entered into the record.

Bria Wilbur was present and represented the owners of the property.

Ms. Wilbur states that the applicants are looking to construct an addition to the existing structure. The addition will exceed 50% of the floor area that existed in the year 2000.

Mr. Cagnetta discussed the history of Roy Carpenter's Beach, including the length of time it took to establish the development into a unique community. He noted that, in 2000, restrictions were placed on the size of structures at 250 Cards Pond Road, as the Zoning Board sought to prevent the construction of excessively large homes. He further acknowledged that this is the first application concerning 240 Cards Pond Road to come before the Zoning Board of Review, which increases the petition's significance.

Ms. Wilbur explains that the applicant, Joshua Smith, and his wife have just recently purchased the property. They also have three children. Noting that the homes in Roy Carpenter's Beach are small to begin with, the applicants are requesting the relief in order to add a second bedroom and enclose a bathroom. The second level will be used for storage only. The proposed design of the addition will keep with the overall aesthetic of the area by squaring the house. The proposed addition will continue to be a minimum of 15 feet away from other cottages.

Board questions ensued.

Mr. Elia points out that the proposed second floor area will include windows and a ladder. Will this eventually be used as a bedroom?

Ms. Wilbur expresses that it will only be used for storage.

Mr. Daniels discussed possible alternative designs for the addition.

Ms. Wilbur concludes that the applicants' design for the addition makes the most sense aesthetically and would allow them the livable area they require.

Ms. Goins clarifies to the board that each future Roy Carpenter's Beach petition will have its own unique structure and characteristics.

Mr. Cagnetta asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak regarding this petition.

There was no one in the audience who wished to speak in favor or in opposition to the petition.

Mr. Cagnetta insisted that originally these were summer cottages with building constraints.

Mr. Gorman says that no structure on 240 Cards Pond Road can be allowed a second story due to height restraints. Lofts are to be used for storage only, nothing habitable. A loft is not included in the footprint or floor area.

Board discussion ensued, and each board member provided their thoughts on this petition as well as possible future petitions of the same kind.

Joshua Smith, applicant, was present and sworn in.

Mr. Smith has lived in the area for over 45 years. He is aware of the restrictions on Roy Carpenter's Beach. This place is symbolic to Mr. Smith, and he doesn't take this application lightly regarding the request for relief.

Mr. Cagnetta expressed reservations, noting that while previous board members worked diligently to establish and preserve the character of the community, approximately 25 years have passed, and community expectations and circumstances may have changed over time.

Mr. Elia asks Mr. Smith what the neighbors thought of the proposed addition.

Mr. Smith answers that all the neighbors have seen the plans and no one has had any issues with it.

Board members each discussed their decisions for this petition.

Ms. Hicks questioned if the applicant had received a letter of approval from the association at Roy Carpenter's Beach. The applicant answered that he had already received approval.

There were no further board questions.

Whereas the following motion was made.

**The Special Use motion is as follows:**

**The following motion to approve the petition was made by Mr. Daniels and duly seconded by Ms. Hicks. Motion passed: (4-1 Vote in favor)**

At a meeting held on October 21, 2026, a motion to approve the special use permit was made regarding **petition ZBR-26-31: Joshua Smith**, 45 West Greenville Rd, Greenville, RI 02828, requests a Special Use Permit and Dimensional Variance under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking to construct a 168 sq. ft. addition to the existing seasonal cottage. The addition will exceed 50% of the floor area that existed in the year 2000. Therefore, relief of 40 sq. ft.is requested. Lot size is 50.2 acres. **A Special Use Permit is required per Zoning Ordinance Section 203 (Special Use Permit for Addition, Enlargement, Expansion or Intensification) and Section 907 (Standards of Relief)**. Owners of cottage 3E C10 are Joshua & Beth Smith, on property owned by RCB Inc, located at 240 Cards Pond Road, South Kingstown, Assessor's Map 92-1, Lot 9-38 and is zoned R200.

### Findings of Fact

1. The Board finds that the special use is specifically authorized by this Ordinance, because the Roy Carpenter's Beach property requires a special use permit before any kind of modification or rebuild to an existing structure.

2. The Board finds that the special use meets all of the criteria set forth in the subsection of this Ordinance authorizing such special use, because Roy Carpenter's Beach is considered a Coastal Community and requires a special use permit be approved before any construction takes place.

3. The Board finds that granting of the special use permit will not alter the general character of the surrounding area or impair the intent or purpose of this Ordinance or the Comprehensive Plan of the Town. In so doing, the Board has considered whether or not satisfactory provisions and arrangements have been or will be made concerning, but not limited to, the following matters, where applicable:

i. Ingress and egress to the lot and to existing or proposed structures thereon with particular reference to automotive and pedestrian safety and convenience, traffic flow and control, and access in case of fire, emergency, or catastrophe; will remain the same with the dimensions of the rear of the property changing slightly. Spacing between units will remain the same.

ii. Off-street parking and loading areas where required, with particular attention to the items in subsection A.1., above, and the noise, glare, or odor effects of the special use permit on adjoining lots; are not a reasonable concern.

iii. Trash, storage, and delivery areas with a particular reference to the items in (i) and (ii) above; already exist on the property.

iv. Utilities, with reference to locations, availability, and compatibility; already exists on the property.

v. Screening and buffering with reference to type, dimensions, and character; are not a reasonable concern.

vi. Signs, if any, and exterior lighting with reference to glare, traffic safety, and compatibility and harmony with lots in the zoning district; none associated with this application.

vii. Required yards and other open space; are not a reasonable concern.

viii. General compatibility with lots in the same or abutting zoning districts; in this cottage community all homes are about the same total square footage. The proposed addition will have the same aesthetics as the surrounding area.

**Approval is conditional subject to the following conditions:**

- There are no conditions upon this approval.

__**The Dimensional Variance motion is as follows**:__
**The following motion to approve the petition was made by Mr. Daniels and duly seconded by Mr. Elia. Motion Passed: (4-1 Vote in favor)**
**(Mr. Daniels -Aye, Mr. Elia -Aye, Mr. MacDonald -Aye, Ms. Hicks -Aye, Mr. Cagnetta -Nay)**

At a meeting held on October 21, 2026, a motion to approve the Dimensional Variance permit was made regarding **petition ZBR-26-31: Joshua Smith**, 45 West Greenville Rd, Greenville, RI 02828, requests a Special Use Permit and Dimensional Variance under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking to construct a 168 sq. ft. addition to the existing seasonal cottage. The addition will exceed 50% of the floor area that existed in the year 2000. Therefore, relief of 40 sq. ft.is requested. Lot size is 50.2 acres. **A Dimensional Variance is required per Section 608 (Coastal Community Overlay District)**. Owners of cottage 3E C10 are Joshua & Beth Smith, on property owned by RCB Inc, located at 240 Cards Pond Road, South Kingstown, Assessor's Map 92-1, Lot 9-38 and is zoned R200.

### Findings of Fact

1. The Board finds that the hardship from which the applicant seeks relief is due to the unique characteristics of the subject land or structure and not to the general characteristics of the surrounding area; and is not due to a physical or economic disability of the applicant, excepting those physical disabilities addressed in § 45-24-30(16), because Roy Carpenter's Beach is a unique location in that it is characterized as a singular property. The requested addition is required to allow for a second bedroom and a larger bathroom. The request for an additional 40 sq. ft. is a minimal amount of relief.

2. The Board finds that the hardship is not the result of any prior action of the applicant, because the applicant has not begun any construction until the dimensional variance is approved.

3. The Board finds that the granting of the requested variance will not alter the general character of the surrounding area or impair the intent or purpose of the zoning ordinance or the comprehensive plan upon which the ordinance is based, because there have already been improvements to other cottages in the area. The addition would enhance the overall appearance and aesthetic appeal of the property.

4. The Board finds that the hardship suffered by the owner of the subject property if the dimensional variance is not granted amounts to more than a mere inconvenience, meaning that relief sought is minimal to a reasonable enjoyment of the permitted use to which the property is proposed to be devoted, because the requested addition is required to allow for a second bedroom and a larger bathroom. Following extensive testimony and discussion with the applicant, the board determined through testimony that the requested proposal could not be accommodated without a significant redesign.

**Approval is conditional subject to the following conditions:**

- There are no conditions upon this approval.

**The following individuals spoke as representatives of the applicant:**

- Bria Wilbur, representing the applicant
- Josh Smith, applicant

**There was no one in the audience who wished to speak in favor or in opposition to the petition.**

**The following materials were entered into the record:**

- "Existing & Proposed Survey" designed by Jackson Surveying, Inc. signed by Charee M. Jackson, P.L.S. and dated August 11, 2026; "Structural Section A Plan" designed by RP Engineering, Inc. signed by Richard L. Pastore, R.P.E. and dated August 11, 2026; "Structural Section B Plan" designed by RP Engineering, Inc. signed by Richard L. Jackson P.L.S. and dated July 15, 2026. (10 pages).
- 200' Abutter's List and Radius Map; Legal Notices; and Notarized Affidavit of Mailing.

Mr. Cagnetta called for the next petition.

IV. **ZBR-26-32: Donald & Pamela Pomeroy**, 135 Park Ave, Wakefield, RI 02879, requests a Dimensional Variance under the Zoning Ordinance as follows: The applicant is seeking to construct multiple additions to the existing dwelling. The additions will be 28' from the front property line and 9.3' from the side property line. The required front and side yard setbacks are 29.4' and 12.6', respectively. Relief of 1.4'(front) and 3.3'(side) are requested. Lot size is .39 acre. **A Dimensional Variance is required per Zoning Ordinance Section 205 (Single Nonconforming Recorded Lots) and Section 907 (Standards of Relief).** Owners of the property are Donald & Pamela Pomeroy for premises located at 135 Park Avenue, South Kingstown, Assessor's Map 92-2, Lot 144 and is zoned R20
135 Park Avenue - Application

All the material was recognized and entered into the record.

Attorney Steven Surdut was present and representing the applicants.

Mr. Surdut begins by saying that the applicants have lived at the address for a long time and that it is their full-time residence. The applicants are looking to turn their three-season home into a year-round house. The proposed addition would give this home a modern architectural design that would fit in with the rest of the neighborhood. The current structure is not centered on the lot making conditions for construction not ideal. The additions include a master suite and a modification to the existing kitchen.

Lorine Foley, an architect who designed the proposed plans, was present and sworn in.

Ms. Foley has been an architectural designer in Southern Rhode Island for about 20 years. The main part of the house was built around the 1900s. The proposed plans will keep this historic part of the structure. At the same time, the additions include an enlarged kitchen, added laundry, pantry, and an expanded master suite. The side setbacks will remain the same and the back of the structure will go back a little deeper. The front deck is existing, and the proposed plans will extend the deck out.

Mr. Cagnetta asks if the proposed plans will encroach any closer to neighboring structures.

Ms. Foley answers that the front will extend outwards more in order to allow for steps to be built.

Mr. Surdut adds that the applicants are only asking for 3.3 feet of relief for the side yard setbacks. The applicants are looking to add a bit of architectural design and usability to their front porch (140 square feet) so they can access it more easily in the front of the structure.

Mr. Cagnetta asks about the other accessory structures located on the property.

The homeowners answer saying that they are sheds. (off microphone)

Mr. Surdut wraps up by saying, essentially, this application is dealing with an old historic structure that was built with lot lines and setbacks which have come into place around it.

Donald Pomeroy, homeowner, was present and sworn in.

Mr. Pomeroy attests that the proposed plans will not encroach any further on surrounding structures. All the accessory buildings on the property are used for storage.

There were no further board questions.

Mr. Cagnetta asked if anyone in the audience would like to speak regarding this petition.

There was no one in the audience who wished to speak in favor or in opposition to the petition.

There was no further board discussion.

### Findings of Fact
